VALIDATED 2026-10-07: F3 (assertions A3+A4+A5+A6) lands the inbound admission gate at the DB layer: handlers/replicated_row.rs::admit_inbound_row resolves the entry author's role from the local tables at the verse scope (role_manager::resolve_role: owner via created_by, explicit role rows, then default_access which the schema pins to viewer/none) and requires Editor+ through the same fe-policy standard write gate as the local path (rbac::evaluate_write) - deny-by-default, never wire-supplied. A bootstrap window admits rows for a verse not yet converged locally (replica capability is the admission; the verse manifest itself arrives this way, so A2 depends on it), and a verse row whose payload verse_id differs from the replica's verse is denied (scope-injection guard). New ReplicatedRowOutcome::Denied variant; denied rows are never applied and never re-emitted. The wire tombstone form (the empty Doc::del entry) now synthesizes the node payload and resolves the scene-change petal from the durable row (empty entries on static hierarchy tables are NotApplicable). Petal bounds apply through the inline numeric literal cast (render_polygon_rings) - a bound GeoJSON object, even under an explicit cast, is rejected by this SurrealDB line. Fixed rbac::get_role to project full rows (the old SELECT role projection made every existing role row fail typed deserialization, so explicit roles never resolved and assign_role_checked for a non-owner Manager errored). fe-sync sync_thread.rs send sweep complete: every SyncEvent send goes through send_sync_event (the last bare .ok()s were the blob/tileset stub handlers; the F1-era startup sends were already converted by F2). Evidence: cargo test -p fe-database 169 passed; cargo test -p fe-sync 133 passed; clippy -D warnings clean on fe-runtime/fe-database/fe-sync/fe-test-harness with fe-ui/fractalengine/fractalengine-relay checked; harness scenario two_peer_tombstone_sync (A5) passes - live node, empty-entry tombstone, stale live row over the real loopback transport with durable READ-BACK each leg, N-4 holds; all 11 harness scenarios green (A2 re-proven with the gate active). Petal namespaces (phase 2), relay lifecycle/bootstrap (F4/A7-A10), gossip receive (phase 3), per-petal topics (phase 4), tileset P2P (phase 5) remain open. Keep in_progress; n0 hosted-relay EOL remains 2026-12-31.VALIDATED 2026-10-07: F4 (assertions A7-A10) lands the relay as a fully applying replica and its ops lifecycle. fractalengine-relay/src/main.rs threads its DbCommand sender into spawn_sync_thread (was None - inbound replicated rows were dropped-and-counted, never applied) and passes the shared FsBlobStore + replication sender into fe_api::ApiConfig (closes the asset-endpoint 503 gap; GUI main.rs wires the same). New fractalengine-relay/src/replicas.rs opens a replica for every hosted verse at startup (one DbCommand::LoadHierarchy round-trip, namespace secret from the relay's EnvBackend secret store, namespace id derived via the DB handler's own keyed blake3 when the row has none) and on every DbResult::VerseCreated; a per-process opened-set stops later HierarchyLoaded replies from churning live replicas. Why a channel round-trip and not a second SurrealKV connection: SurrealKV takes a per-handle file lock, so a second in-process connection cannot coexist with the DB thread's writer on Windows (os error 33; fe-database's own examples note the app must not be running) - the relay's api_db_reader legitimately falls back to the channel there, same as the GUI. Opening a replica runs fe-sync's startup reconciliation pass (replicator.rs VerseReplicator::snapshot over get_many single_latest_per_key -> the same inbound apply path), so rows the A3 role gate denied while a role or the verse manifest had not yet converged get a second chance on every open - 3 new fe-sync tests. Graceful shutdown: SIGINT/SIGTERM (and FE_SHUTDOWN_AFTER_SECS for windowed runs) sends DbCommand::Shutdown + SyncCommand::Shutdown, waits 750ms, and a Bevy system raises AppExit::Success so app.run() returns and the process exits 0 - verified e2e (cmd %ERRORLEVEL% capture: exit 0 on fresh DB, existing DB, and bootstrap runs). FE_SYNC_BOOTSTRAP (A9) is parsed with iroh's own serde NodeAddr types: e2e shows the invalid entry warned loudly and skipped, the valid NodeAddr JSON resolved (count=1) and start_sync'd per replica (Opened verse replica peers=1). The DB->sync bridge is extracted to run_replication_bridge with try_send + drop-and-warn (dropped_total) and a prompt-return unit test on a full channel (A10); no bare .ok() in touched paths. Two pre-existing relay defects fixed en route: (1) drain_sync_events needs fe_sync::TilesetEventBuffer, which only fe-ui inits - the relay panicked on its first frame (Resource does not exist) since its inception; (2) no headless system delivered DbResults to pending API requests (the GUI's fe-ui dispatcher does it), so every channel-fallback API request (/ready Ping, hierarchy reads, scope resolutions) timed out - new fe_runtime::app::deliver_pending_api_results (relay-registered) fixed /ready 503 -> 200 in e2e. Evidence: cargo test -p fractalengine-relay 6 passed (startup_scan_opens_replicas_from_hierarchy_loaded, verse_created_opens_replica_with_derived_namespace, replication_bridge_drops_and_warns_on_full_channel, shutdown_flag_raises_app_exit_success, 2 namespace derivation tests); cargo fmt clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace exit 0 (0 failed); harness scenarios 11 passed 0 failed. A7 caveat, recorded honestly: two LIVE relay processes converging rows was not run end-to-end - the relay exposes no unauthenticated write surface (all REST/MCP writes are JWT-gated and token minting is UI-only), so a cross-relay write needs an invite/join contract outside F4; the convergence seam itself (same spawn_sync_thread + inbound apply path + bootstrap address form) is proven by the harness two_peer_replica_sync scenario over the real loopback transport. FUTURE-HARDENING (from F3, recorded per conductor directive): the A3 gate confines a row to the replica's verse but does not verify cross-verse references - an Editor admitted in verse A can push non-verse rows referencing verse B's ids (e.g. a node row whose petal/fractal ids belong to another verse); full referential-confinement checking was out of F3's scope and is documented in the gate's doc comments (handlers/replicated_row.rs) - add referential checking to the admission gate when the verse-manifest/role bootstrap contract is specified. Phases 2 (petal namespaces), 3 (gossip receive), 4 (per-petal topics), 5 (tileset P2P) remain open. Keep in_progress; n0 hosted-relay EOL remains 2026-12-31.
VALIDATED 2026-10-07: F20 (M1 scrutiny round-1, feature F20-m1-replication-hardening) repairs the four confirmed blocking defects from validation/M1/scrutiny/synthesis.json (reviews F2/F4, evidence verified at tree 853af53). (1) Reconciliation self-deadlock: seed_reconciliation no longer awaits per-entry sends into the 256-capacity aggregated inbound channel whose only drainer is the command loop running it - snapshot entries now apply DIRECTLY through handle_inbound_row_change (try_send drop-and-count, the literal same inbound apply path); the regression test sync_thread::tests::reconciliation_snapshot_larger_than_inbound_capacity_does_not_deadlock proves a 300-entry doc on a REAL sync thread (> channel capacity) converges live, replays the full snapshot on re-open, and Shutdown still processes (Stopped + clean join). The self-drain rule is documented in fe-sync/src/AGENTS.md. (2) Entry-author identity: docs_engine.rs DocsStack::spawn imports the endpoint SecretKey as the docs author (authors().import + set_default), so entry.author() resolves to the endpoint NodeId did:key == fe DID (to_iroh_seed shares the seed); the live pump AND the snapshot attribute RowChange.author_id from entry.author() (author_did_key) - never InsertRemote.from (the forwarding neighbor, which made >=3-member docs judge the relaying node instead of the author and made the mandated second-chance replay deny again through a role-less per-dir default author). Test doc_replicator_replicates_row_over_real_transport asserts live author == snapshot author == alice's endpoint did:key; fe-database denied_row_converges_on_replay_after_role_lands proves a role-denied row converges on restart replay under the one identity; already_applied_row_redelivery_stays_applied proves re-delivery of pre-F20-authored entries stays harmless. (3) Namespace ids: fe_database::derive_namespace_id now returns the Ed25519 verifying key of the secret (the id iroh registers the doc under), so the secretless reopen client.open(stored_id) finds a previously imported doc on the same persisted store; legacy keyed-BLAKE3 ids in live DBs fall back to find_doc_by_verse_manifest (scan of known docs for the verse/{id} manifest key); tests secretless_reopen_finds_persisted_doc_by_aligned_id, secretless_reopen_falls_back_to_manifest_scan_on_legacy_id, secretless_open_with_no_matching_doc_fails_loudly, derive_namespace_id_matches_iroh_namespace_id pin the shapes; create_verse/invite handlers derive via the same fn so new rows store the aligned id; relay replicas.rs and the harness scenarios derive via the same fn so their tests stay truthful. (4) Mock fallback on online open errors (orchestrator ruling: the approved contract text governs): mock fallback is offline-only (is_available() == false); on an ONLINE stack a failed open marks the replica loudly non-replicating - new SyncEvent::ReplicaOpenFailed (drain arm in status.rs), an error! open banner saying NOT replicating, write_row/subscribe/snapshot all erroring (tests marked_failed_replica_is_loudly_non_replicating, online_open_failure_leaves_loud_non_replicating_replica, offline_open_failure_keeps_mock_fallback); fe-sync/src/AGENTS.md §iroh-0.35 updated (the broader unusable-capability mock form removed). Fold-ins: inbound verse manifests with default_access outside {viewer,none} are Denied in apply_static_row (negative test inbound_verse_manifest_with_editor_default_access_is_denied + positive none-applies test); the relay Seed send is no longer a bare .ok() (error + exit 1, the GUI seed-gate pattern); the relay opened-set is now a shared OpenedReplicas resource across the startup scan and VerseCreated systems (runtime-created verses no longer churned close+reopen by the next HierarchyLoaded - the verse_created test extended to prove no-churn). BOARD CORRECTIONS (F20 conductor pass): (a) the F3 note above claims default_access 'which the schema pins to viewer/none' - FALSE as stated: fe-database schema.rs:143 is a column DEFAULT 'viewer', not an ASSERT; the real inbound pin landed with F20 in apply_static_row's validation (fe-database/src/AGENTS.md §handlers third rule documents it). (b) the F4 FUTURE-HARDENING note says the confinement gap 'is documented in the gate's doc comments (handlers/replicated_row.rs)' - at F4 time that text existed only in this note; F20 added the actual doc comment to admit_inbound_row, so the pointer is now true. Evidence: cargo test -p fe-database 176 passed (11 ignored, pre-existing) plus all integration suites green; cargo test -p fe-sync 145 passed; cargo test -p fractalengine-relay 6 passed; cargo clippy -p fe-sync -p fe-database -p fractalengine-relay --all-targets -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean; harness scenarios 11 passed 0 failed (FE_SYNC_RELAY=disabled - A2/A5 re-proven over the new author attribution and aligned ids). Phases 2 (petal namespaces), 3 (gossip receive), 4 (per-petal topics), 5 (tileset P2P) remain open. Keep in_progress; n0 hosted-relay EOL remains 2026-12-31.
